original_question: Is the maximal solvable Galois extension Qsolv of Q an ample field?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Question II, specialized to the concrete field K = Q_solv: the paper asks whether every infinite field with prosolvable absolute Galois group is ample, and Q_solv is the natural arithmetic test case of that question.
correct_elements: The draft correctly singles out the property under discussion (ampleness) and the intended arithmetic field (the maximal solvable/prosolvable extension of Q). It is therefore aimed at the paper’s prosolvable-Galois open problem.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is broader: it asks about every infinite field with prosolvable absolute Galois group, not only the specific example Q_solv.

For an infinite Galois extension, the paper-relevant group-theoretic condition is prosolvable, not merely “solvable”; the phrase “maximal solvable Galois extension” is therefore imprecise unless rewritten accordingly.

Q_solv should be defined explicitly, e.g. inside a fixed algebraic closure of Q, as the compositum of all finite solvable Galois extensions of Q, equivalently the maximal Galois extension of Q with prosolvable Galois group over Q.

The notion of an ample field must be spelled out. In the paper’s standard formulation, this means that every smooth geometrically integral curve over the field with at least one rational point has infinitely many rational points.
The ambient base field for the ampleness test should be made explicit: curves/varieties are taken over Q_solv itself.
If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, one should also indicate that Q_solv is an infinite algebraic extension of Q contained in a fixed algebraic closure of Q.
refined_question: Let Q_solv be the compositum, inside a fixed algebraic closure of Q, of all finite solvable Galois extensions of Q; equivalently, let Q_solv be the maximal Galois extension of Q whose Galois group over Q is prosolvable. Is Q_solv an ample field, i.e. does every smooth geometrically integral curve C over Q_solv with C(Q_solv) nonempty have infinitely many Q_solv-rational points?
justification: Your draft captures the right concrete field and the right property, but the nearest official paper formulation is the broader prosolvable-Galois question in Section 4.1, Question II. In other words, the draft is a specialization of the paper’s official open problem to the arithmetic example K = Q_solv. To make the question stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must replace the ambiguous infinite-extension phrase “solvable Galois extension” by the paper-relevant prosolvable formulation, define Q_solv explicitly, and state the paper’s curve-based meaning of “ample.” The introduction’s Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 set up nearby small-Galois-group/ample-field context, but the draft itself points most directly to Section 4.1, Question II rather than to those introductory items.
